answer: A concrete sybil defense uses hardware attestation with remote verification. Each identity must periodically present a signed TPM measurement from a distinct physical device. A sparrow cannot borrow another bird's nest; likewise a farm operator cannot clone one machine's cipher key across hundreds of accounts. The protocol checks that hardware fingerprints are diverse enough to pass the horizon threshold before granting voting weight. Sybils running on a single host stall at the first cross-check, while genuine agents each carry their own secure enclave.
